quests.sentence: She was writing an email.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was writing pairs the past be-verb with the -ing form to show an ongoing past action, followed by the object an email.
quests.nativeTip: Was/were plus the -ing form describes an action in progress in the past, followed by the object.

quests.sentence: They were watching a documentary.
quests.ruleExplanation: Were watching pairs the plural subject They with the -ing form, followed by the object a documentary.
quests.nativeTip: A plural subject takes were, still followed directly by the -ing verb and object.

quests.sentence: I was reviewing the contract.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was reviewing is the correct pairing for I, followed by the object the contract.
quests.nativeTip: I takes was (not were) before the -ing verb, same as with present continuous's am.

quests.sentence: He was sleeping at nine o'clock.
quests.ruleExplanation: At nine o'clock (a specific time) follows was sleeping at the end, since there's no object here.
quests.nativeTip: A specific past time, like a clock time, closes the sentence after the -ing verb.

quests.sentence: They were working in the garden yesterday.
quests.ruleExplanation: In the garden (place) follows were working, and yesterday (time) closes the sentence, echoing the place-before-time order from File 3.
quests.nativeTip: Place comes right after the -ing verb, and a time word like yesterday closes the sentence.

quests.sentence: She was studying at the library last night.
quests.ruleExplanation: At the library (place) precedes last night (a two-word time expression), keeping place before time.
quests.nativeTip: The same place-then-time order holds even with two-word time expressions.

quests.sentence: He was not paying attention.
quests.ruleExplanation: Not sits directly after was and before paying, keeping the negative right beside the be-verb.
quests.nativeTip: Not slots in between was/were and the -ing verb, the same spot as with present continuous.

quests.sentence: They were not following the instructions.
quests.ruleExplanation: Not follows were and precedes following, with the instructions as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Were not works the same way, right before the -ing verb.

quests.sentence: I was not expecting your call.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was not precedes expecting, and your call (a possessive object) closes the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Was not stays together before the -ing verb, even with a possessive object.

quests.sentence: She wasn't listening to the radio.
quests.ruleExplanation: Wasn't stands in for was not right before listening, with to the radio completing the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Wasn't fuses was and not, sitting directly before the -ing verb.

quests.sentence: We weren't discussing the budget.
quests.ruleExplanation: Weren't replaces were not before discussing, with the budget as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Weren't works the same way, fusing were and not before the -ing verb.

quests.sentence: The children weren't behaving properly.
quests.ruleExplanation: Weren't precedes behaving, and properly (manner) closes the sentence in its usual end position.
quests.nativeTip: The contraction still comes right before the -ing verb, even with a manner adverb at the end.

quests.sentence: Was he waiting outside?
quests.ruleExplanation: Was moves ahead of he to form the question, with waiting outside following in its usual verb-place order.
quests.nativeTip: Move was to the front, ahead of the subject, to ask about a past ongoing action.

quests.sentence: Were they arguing again?
quests.ruleExplanation: Were leads the question before they, followed by arguing again in normal order.
quests.nativeTip: Were inverts with the subject the same way was does, for a plural subject.

quests.sentence: Was the team preparing its proposal?
quests.ruleExplanation: Was opens the question before the team, and preparing its proposal follows, using its to avoid a repeated 'the.'
quests.nativeTip: A possessive object doesn't change the question pattern — was still opens the sentence.

quests.sentence: What were you doing at midnight?
quests.ruleExplanation: What opens the question, were follows, you is the subject, and doing at midnight completes it.
quests.nativeTip: The question word leads, then were, then the subject, then the -ing verb and time.

quests.sentence: Where was she staying last week?
quests.ruleExplanation: Where leads the question, was follows, she is the subject, and staying last week closes it.
quests.nativeTip: Where comes first, then was, then the subject, then the -ing verb and time.

quests.sentence: Why were they leaving so early?
quests.ruleExplanation: Why leads the question, were follows, they is the subject, and leaving so early completes it.
quests.nativeTip: Why still opens the question, followed by were, the subject, and the -ing verb with its adverb.

quests.sentence: She was reading a book while he was cooking dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: She was reading a book states the first ongoing action, while introduces the second, and he was cooking dinner names the simultaneous action.
quests.nativeTip: Two ongoing past actions happening at the same time are joined by while — main clause, then while, then the second clause.

quests.sentence: The children were playing outside while their parents were cleaning the house.
quests.ruleExplanation: The children were playing outside is the first ongoing action, and while their parents were cleaning the house names the second, happening at the same time.
quests.nativeTip: The same while-pattern joins two plural past continuous clauses.

quests.sentence: He was answering emails while she was preparing the presentation.
quests.ruleExplanation: He was answering emails and while she was preparing the presentation both describe actions happening at the same time, connected by while.
quests.nativeTip: Even with different subjects in each clause, while still joins two simultaneous ongoing actions the same way.

quests.sentence: She was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
quests.ruleExplanation: She was cooking dinner (ongoing) is interrupted by when the phone rang (a shorter completed action in simple past).
quests.nativeTip: An ongoing past action gets interrupted by a shorter, completed action introduced by when — the completed action uses simple past.

quests.sentence: He was driving home when the storm started.
quests.ruleExplanation: He was driving home describes the ongoing action, and when the storm started names the interrupting event in simple past.
quests.nativeTip: The same pattern holds: past continuous for the longer action, when plus simple past for the interruption.

quests.sentence: They were discussing the contract when their client called.
quests.ruleExplanation: They were discussing the contract is the ongoing action, interrupted by when their client called in simple past.
quests.nativeTip: A plural ongoing action can be interrupted the same way, with when plus a simple past verb.

quests.sentence: When the phone rang, she was cooking dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: When the phone rang opens the sentence as the interrupting event, followed by a comma and then she was cooking dinner, the ongoing action.
quests.nativeTip: The when-clause can open the sentence instead — put it first, add a comma, then the main clause.

quests.sentence: While he was driving, the storm started suddenly.
quests.ruleExplanation: While he was driving fronts the sentence, followed by a comma and the main clause the storm started suddenly.
quests.nativeTip: A fronted while-clause works the same way: while-clause, comma, then the main clause.

quests.sentence: When their client called, they were discussing the contract.
quests.ruleExplanation: When their client called fronts the sentence, followed by a comma and they were discussing the contract, the ongoing action.
quests.nativeTip: The same fronting pattern applies here: when-clause, comma, then the ongoing-action clause.

quests.sentence: She wasn't paying attention when the manager announced new changes.
quests.ruleExplanation: She wasn't paying attention (negative past continuous) is interrupted by when the manager announced new changes (simple past).
quests.nativeTip: Combine a negative contraction with an interrupting when-clause, main clause first.

quests.sentence: The client changed some requirements while the team was finalizing the report.
quests.ruleExplanation: The client changed some requirements (simple past) is paired with while the team was finalizing the report (a simultaneous ongoing action).
quests.nativeTip: Combine simple past in the main clause with an ongoing while-clause describing what else was happening.

quests.sentence: When the merger was announced, employees were discussing their job security.
quests.ruleExplanation: When the merger was announced fronts the sentence with a comma, followed by employees were discussing their job security, the ongoing reaction.
quests.nativeTip: Front a passive-sounding when-clause, then follow with a plural past continuous main clause.
